I need to find a maximal triangle-free graph on 16 vertices. A maximal triangle-free graph is one where adding any new edge would create a triangle.

The Turán graph T(16,2) = K(8,8) is the densest triangle-free graph on 16 vertices, and it's also maximal (it's a complete bipartite graph, so adding any edge within a partition would create a triangle... wait, K(8,8) has no edges within partitions, and adding one would create a triangle only if two vertices in the same partition have a common neighbor - which they do in K(8,8)).

Let me verify K(8,8) is maximal triangle-free:
- It's bipartite, so triangle-free ✓
- Adding any edge (u,v) where u,v are in the same partition: since every vertex in one partition connects to all 8 vertices in the other partition, u and v share all 8 neighbors in the opposite partition, so adding edge (u,v) creates triangles ✓

So K(8,8) with partitions {0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7} and {8,9,10,11,12,13,14,15} works.
